$schema_note: Cold-start happy paths consulted before asking the model. Fields documented in LLM/docs/supervisor/BOOTSTRAP.md 'Cold-start recipe table'. Profile order matters — the first match wins, so list newer/narrower architectures BEFORE broader fallbacks.

profiles.description: NVIDIA Blackwell (RTX 50-series, compute capability >= 10.0). Needs CUDA 12.8+ wheels; cu121 will silently fail at kernel launch because Blackwell's SM_100 isn't compiled into the cu121 builds.
NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.1+ runtime, compute capability 8.0-9.x (Ampere RTX 30 / Ada RTX 40 / Hopper).
Turing (RTX 20-series, compute 7.5) — CUDA 11.8 + torch 2.4. cu121 wheels also work on Turing but 11.8 is what's been smoke-tested in production.

Pascal (GTX 10-series, compute 6.1). Newer torch versions drop SM_61 from prebuilt wheels — pinning to torch 2.2 keeps inference working; training is best-effort. Ask the user before assuming this is the right path because the upgrade story is bumpy.

args.question: Detected an older Pascal-generation NVIDIA GPU (GTX 10-series). Modern torch wheels have limited support for this hardware — training will be unreliable, inference works. Continue with the legacy profile?

profiles.description: No discrete GPU — install CPU-only torch and warn the user that training will be slow.

args.question: No GPU detected — training will run on CPU and be very slow. Continue?
